text:
Re: Golden v. Watson volume

1. Targets are earned - Golden has been getting open constantly, not force fed

2. Golden is a much better man beater than Watson, while both are good against zone. Nearly the entirety of the target gap between the two comes from their difference in volume vs. man coverage.

3. While both get targeted deep downfield on average, Watson is targeted further downfield on average (15 vs. 13.5 aDOT). Further downfield targets = less overall volume generally, and both are targeted at an elite rate given their aDOTs

quote.text:
I can't deny that, despite his drops, Matthew Golden has been impressive and exceeded all expectations this season

But at what point do the Packers stop force-feeding him targets in the hope that his brick hands just disappear? 

Golden leads the league with 13 drops, 5 more than the next closest WR (per @FantasyPtsData) 

You know who hasn't had any drop issues this season? Christian Watson 

In fact, Watson has the most targets of any WR without recording a single dropped pass (75)

And that isn't the only area where Watson has been much better than Golden... 

YPRR :  2.99 to 2.55 
Passer Rating :  136.3 to 92.1 
Explosive Reception Rate :  36.2% to 30.9% 
Contested Catch Rate :  61.9% to 27.3% 
YPTOE :  3.30 to -0.10 
EPA/Target :  0.7474 to 0.286

It's not like Golden is getting open at a much higher rate than Watson either — 0.088 ASS to 0.077 and 14.3% Route Win Rate to 13.1%
